thesis: A reported fuel or CO2 saving against a great-circle baseline is not identifiable until the network effect, the speed-policy effect, and the weather effect are reported separately.

formulas.network_effect_interpretation: Positive means the feasible coastline-masked path uses more fuel than the great-circle baseline at the same speed. The great-circle figure understates a feasible voyage. It is not a saving.
formulas.speed_policy_deadline_interpretation: Under calm water and a convex fuel-speed curve, this is zero if the deadline speed equals the service speed on the same path.
formulas.speed_policy_commercial_interpretation: Depends on the stated bunker price and charter rate. Not comparable to a fixed-arrival speed schedule.
formulas.weather_effect_status: not_estimated until a frozen hindcast cache exists. Must not be filled with a synthetic field and then called ERA5 or Copernicus.

kill_criteria: Do not report a weather saving if B4.status is not_estimated.
Do not report a percentage against B1 alone.
Do not retune fouling, bunker price, grid resolution, or the strait mask after seeing a ratio, in order to manufacture a saving.
If the only large ratio is a great circle that crosses a continent, call it baseline infeasibility, not optimizer skill.
A positive weather result on one hand-picked corridor is not a result. Weather is not estimated in this revision, so this criterion is not applicable yet.
what_this_file_does_not_authorize: Calling the genetic algorithm a contribution.
Citing Shipping_Lanes_v1.geojson as navigable water or as AIS.
Using the word validated for a model-versus-model comparison.
